items.title: Karnataka SIR: Age gaps, name mismatches among criteria as 20 lakh voters face notices
items.summary: The Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer’s office has listed nine criteria for flagging voters under “anomalies” or “logical discrepancies” during the ongoing SIR. More than 20 lakh electors in Karnataka have been flagged under this category and will receive notices seeking clarification. The criteria relate largely to inconsistencies in the way an elector’s details have been mapped to the previous SIR electoral rolls, including differences in names, unusual age gaps between family members and discrepancies in parent-child relationships. The criteria assume significance, as Karnataka’s draft electoral roll, published on August 24, has 4,46,80,151 electors. Of these, 20,35,835 have been categorised as having anomalies or logical discrepancies, while another 23,45,500 have been placed in the no-mapping category. Together, 43,81,335 electors, or 9.82% of the draft electorate, are set to receive notices. According to the criteria issued by the CEO’s office, an elector can be flagged if the age difference between them and a parent to whom they have been linked is less than 15 years or more than 50 years. items.title: Who will lead India’s next student movement?
items.summary: In this episode of What's Your ISM?, TNM Executive Editor Sudipto Mondal sits down with student leaders from the All India Students’ Association (AISA) and Ambedkar Students’ Association (ASA) to discuss the new opportunities to build student politics, the growing anger on Indian campuses, and the possibilities and contradictions within today’s student movements. Sudipto and the student leaders also explore the relationship between caste and class politics, Ambedkar and Marx, the Left and Ambedkarite movements, and whether these forces can find common ground. They discuss the recent student protests, the rise of Gen Z politics, the education crisis, privatisation, unemployment, and the demand for student union elections in Karnataka. The conversation also looks at whether student organisations can build a third front beyond the BJP and Congress, the challenges of organising across caste and class lines, and the role of ideology in sustaining a movement beyond a single protest. They also discuss the Rohith Act campaign in Karnataka, and how different student organisations came together to push for stronger protections against discrimination in universities. The course will be conducted between October 9 and 10, 2026, followed by an international conference on October 11. items.title: A year after Israeli strikes killed journalists at a hospital, no one has been held accountable
items.summary: It’s been a year since Israeli soldiers killed 22 Palestinians , including journalists and rescue workers, in a double strike on a hospital in Gaza. No one has been held accountable. Israeli officials said the target was a suspected Hamas camera on the roof of Nasser Hospital. Among those killed were Reuters cameraman Hussam al-Masri and Mariam Dagga , a visual journalist who worked for The Associated Press and other news organisations. Despite repeated requests by AP , the army hasn’t provided details about the investigation or a timeline for when it could be completed. Rights groups say Israel rarely holds troops accountable for killing Palestinians, pointing to long investigations that rarely lead to prosecution . As global outrage over the August 25, 2025, strikes grew, the Israeli military said that in addition to taking out the camera, six of those killed were linked to Hamas, without providing evidence. But an Israeli soldier, speaking on condition of anonymity for fear of retribution, now says the military could find no evidence linking the camera, which belonged to al-Masri, to Hamas. items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently questioned why Indian women are expected to take permission from members of the matrimonial home to visit their own parents' home. Justice Chillakur Sumalatha said that wives cannot be expected to solely do household work. "This Court does not understand why an Indian woman is required to take permission of all present at her matrimonial home to fulfil her basic desire of visiting her parents house as and when she wish and feels to go. This Court is of the view that anyone including husband cannot command and demand any female including his wife to do the household activities and to look after, his parents." The duty of taking care of parents vests upon the son or the daughter and not on the son-in-law or daughter-in-law, the Court added. Reiterating the choice every woman has, the Court said, "A woman has fundamental and absolute right to make decisions concerning her career, finances, etc. Huband cannot compel wife or coerce her to live according to his wishes and expectations. But Lantana camara, which now occupies 40% of India’s tiger habitats, was not the only one. items.title: Delhi High Court gives slum dwellers near PM Modi's residence 6 weeks to move to DUSIB colony
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Tuesday directed the residents of three slum clusters near Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence in the Race Course area to vacate within 6 weeks and move to the alternative location provided by government authorities. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia said that after 6 weeks, the government can clear the land with the help of the police. "The appellants shall vacate the dwelling in the three jhuggi jhopris within six weeks from today. And within this period, they shall be provided with the accommodations allotted to them in DUSIB Colony. Whereafter, they shall be evicted to clear the land, if necessary, with the assistance of the police," the Court ordered. It ruled that there had been no violation of the rehabilitation policy in moving the residents in this case. Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia However, the Division Bench said that the government will be bound by its undertakings and the Court's previous orders requiring availability of amenities at DUSIB Colony .
